chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the eye of the one-eyed person, the blood money (diyah) is complete.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Blood money or compensation for bodily injury or death
key_terms.عَيْنِ الْأَعْوَرِ: The eye of the one-eyed person (referring to the remaining functional eye)
key_terms.كَامِلَةٌ: Complete or full (referring to the full amount of diyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money compensation for injuring the remaining eye of a person who is already one-eyed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'complete compensation' for the loss of the final functional sense, establishing that the remaining eye holds the same value as both eyes combined in terms of diya. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the impairment of the last eye constitutes a total loss of vision, thereby triggering the full blood money payment rather than a partial deduction for the initial defect.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘With regards to an eye of the one-eyed, is the complete wergild’.
